cells.uncertainty: Pilot cell: two third-party paths, jansson 2.15.1 (282,984 Debian popcon sourcemax installations) and json-c 0.19 (269,736), both captured 2026-11-17, were built, control-verified against the exact nested structure of the control, and given native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. They are separate parser families: jansson's recursive-descent src/load.c and json-c's incremental state-machine json_tokener.c. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'json' (24 hits, 3 of them C JSON parsers) plus three targeted C names (jansson, jsmn, parson); adoption was compared with Debian popcon sourcemax counts. cJSON (150,958) and yyjson (14,868) were not built. Popcon counts Debian installations of the library packages, mostly pulled in as dependencies, not developer choice; the jansson/json-c gap (13,248, under 5%) is too small to read as a preference. parson has no Debian package and no comparable number. Conan and Debian do not cover vendored single-file copies (common for cJSON). ISO C documents no JSON API. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell: JsonCpp 1.9.8 and nlohmann/json 3.12.0 were built and control-verified. Popcon measures Debian installs; JsonCpp's runtime count is inflated by dependents such as CMake, and header-only libraries (nlohmann/json, RapidJSON) have only dev packages, so popcon undercounts them. GitHub stars rank nlohmann/json first (50,894 vs 8,916). simdjson is above nlohmann/json at popcon source level (2,688 vs 1,799) through its runtime library but was not built. Eight leads are logged in leads.json and are not selected or ranked. Framework packages (Qt, Boost, POCO) are not ranked by whole-framework installs. The ISO C++ standard library has no JSON API. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell: two general-purpose JSON decoders were built and control-verified: github.com/json-iterator/go (18,454 Imported by) and github.com/goccy/go-json (4,192). gjson (10,420) was passed over as a non-validating path-query API and ugorji/go/codec (10,142) as a multi-format codec whose Imported by count is not JSON-specific. Seven further numeric leads are logged in leads.json and are not selected or ranked. Non-parser hits such as loggers, JWT, JSON-RPC, and protobuf JSON mappers were not treated as leads. Valid nested-object and nested-array controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell: the two highest-adoption general-purpose JSON parser leads from independent parser families were built and control-verified: jackson-databind (162,890 deps.dev direct dependents summed over 239 releases) and gson (33,240 over 45 releases). jackson-core, the second-highest lead (80,053), is the tokenizer jackson-databind drives, so it stays a same-family lead rather than a separate path. Maven Central text search ranks by relevance, not adoption, so leads were looked up directly on deps.dev; the remaining eleven are logged in leads.json and are not selected or ranked. The Jackson adapter disables CANONICALIZE_FIELD_NAMES for deterministic feedback; Gson uses its default instance. Java SE 25 exports no JSON parsing API, so the standard count is zero by inventory, not by omission. Valid nested object and nested array controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell: one third-party path (stream-json 3.9.0, 56,997,988 npm downloads 2026-10-17 to 2026-11-15) was built, control-verified, and given parser-derived V8 AFL++ feedback. It is the highest-download lead found with its own RFC 8259 tokenizer and a documented local Buffer/stream API. jsonparse (105,362,611) has its own Buffer parser but no documented API and was not selected; json5, jsonc-parser, and json-bigint have higher downloads but string-only APIs and/or superset grammars. Six high-download packages delegate to JSON.parse. Downloads were fetched for 24 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit. The standard JSON.parse path is counted separately; V8 parses it natively, so it has a control receipt and a staged function-entry AFL++ proxy, but no parser source lines or V8 basic-block edges. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell: PHP JSON parsing is dominated by the bundled ext/json json_decode; most popular Packagist JSON packages wrap it. Only seld/jsonlint, the highest-download package with its own pure-PHP parser, was built and control-verified. Its downloads are inflated by Composer, which depends on it but calls json_decode first and uses JsonParser for error reports. Seven own-parser or partial-own-parser leads are logged in leads.json and are not verified or ranked; four json_decode wrappers are excluded. Non-parser hits such as JWT, JSON Schema, JSONPath, JMESPath, serializers and JSON-RPC were not treated as leads. One valid nested object control does not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

This is a one-parser pilot, not a completed popularity search or top-ten claim. Nine named package leads were inspected via PyPI/project documentation; the bounded PyPI Simple Index name search remains pending. Eight leads have no pinned control result. The verified Python standard path explicitly selects the pure-Python json decoder/scanner; CPython's default built-in _json accelerator is not covered or ranked. PyPI Stats downloads are package-level adoption signals, not JSON-specific use.

Pilot cell: one verified path, chosen as the highest crates.io 90-day download count (438,065,825) among all 476 unique search hits. 20 JSON parser leads remain unverified (top: aws-smithy-json 59,322,077, simd-json 6,730,588, jiter 5,274,664), so the count of one reflects pilot scope, not a search result. Search covers only the first 100 hits of six queries (600 hits, 476 unique) captured 2026-11-17; the 'json' query alone reports 55195 matches. Recent downloads include transitive dependency pulls and are an adoption proxy. Superset formats (JSON5, JSONC, Hjson) are excluded. Two small valid UTF-8 controls do not establish duplicate-key, large-number precision, deep-nesting limit (serde_json's default recursion limit is 128), lone-surrogate, or non-UTF-8 behaviour. The Rust 1.99.1 standard library documents no JSON API.

One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for seven queries, captured 2026-11-17; it misses header-only decoders that are not packaged there. minimp3 and dr_mp3 have no value on the primary metric, so their GitHub stars are recorded as supplemental only and are not compared with Homebrew counts. libmad is an unresolved independent family. Homebrew installs measure macOS/Linux package demand for the whole mpg123 distribution (player and library), not direct use of the decoding API. libmpg123 is the same engine counted under mp3_id3v2/c. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for six queries, captured 2026-11-17; header-only C++ decoders and vcpkg/Conan packages were not searched. Homebrew installs measure demand for the whole TagLib distribution, mostly as a tag library, not use of its MPEG property API. TagLib parses frame headers and does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/VBRI its duration comes from stream size and the first frame's bitrate. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

One verified path; no padding. Search is bounded by five pkg.go.dev queries at 100 hits each. Leads in leads.json are not verified parsers. Two valid controls do not establish complete Layer III support or independence from the mp3_id3v2 go-mp3 entry.

Pilot cell: only the highest-adoption pure-Java Layer III path was built and control-verified; no padding. Maven Central Solr search ranks by relevance, the phrase queries 'mp3 decoder' and 'mpeg audio' returned 0 hits, so leads were looked up directly on deps.dev and logged in leads.json. deps.dev public coverage is incomplete and jcodec's count covers the whole codec library, not MP3 use alone. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5 or intensity-stereo support; jcodec's Mp3Decoder throws on intensity stereo by design. Java SE 25 exports no MP3 API, so the standard count is zero by inventory.

One verified path; no padding. Search is six npm queries of 100 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; downloads were fetched for 15 hand-picked candidates, not every hit. mediabunny was found by `mp3 frame`, `mp3 duration` and `mp3 demuxer`, not the narrower queries. Its download count covers the whole media toolkit (muxing, conversion, many containers), not MP3 demuxing alone. The path demuxes frames and reads headers but does not decode Layer III audio (that would need WebCodecs). mediabunny is not among the mp3_id3v2/javascript paths; music-metadata and the mpg123 WASM wrappers are recorded as shared-family leads. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support. No standard Node.js MP3 API exists.

One verified path; no padding. Search is seven Packagist search.json queries capped at 50 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; package descriptions alone decided most exclusions. Packagist total downloads count Composer installs of the whole package (and wrappers pull getID3 transitively), not use of the MPEG frame parser. getID3 reads the first frame header, checks sync on following frames, and derives CBR duration from audio-data bytes and the header bitrate; it does not decode audio or report a frame count on these controls. Mp3Info, PHP-MP3 (falahati/php-mp3), the Zend media reader and fobilow/mp3file are unresolved independent candidates. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

One verified path; no padding. The name search is a substring filter over the PyPI Simple index (serial 43764887) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' and 'mpeg' hit lists were not triaged one by one, and download numbers were fetched only for 13 named candidates, so a less obvious frame parser could be missed. Native wrappers (av, soundfile, audioread, pygame, pymediainfo, miniaudio) are unresolved, not rejected: their parsers are real but outside Python source coverage. tinytag, eyed3, hachoir and pymp3 are unresolved pure-Python leads. Mutagen reads headers and checks frame syncs but does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/Info/VBRI its duration is stream bytes divided by the first header's bitrate. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Pilot cell: one verified path, chosen as the highest crates.io 90-day download count (10,651,437) among hits that contain an MPEG audio frame parser. The facade crate symphonia (11,469,426) ranks higher but re-exports the same family. 11 frame-level leads remain unverified, so the count of one reflects pilot scope, not a search result. Search covers only the first 100 hits of six queries (591 hits, 350 unique) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' query alone reports 1119 matches. Recent downloads include transitive dependency pulls (Symphonia is a dependency of rodio and others) and are an adoption proxy, not evidence of direct MP3 parsing use. Two untagged CBR controls (MPEG-1 44.1 kHz mono, MPEG-2 22.05 kHz stereo) do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Pilot cell: two third-party paths (expat 2.10.0 and libxml2 2.15.4) were built, matched the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls under LLVM source coverage, and have native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. They are distinct parser families. expat leads libxml2 by 6,410 installs (2.2%) on the binary-package metric, a near tie. The Debian sourcemax table would invert the order (libxml2 source 61,109) only because the libxml2 source now builds libxml2-16 and the older libxml2 binary is no longer attributed to it, so binary runtime-library counts are the primary metric; libxml2-16 (9,413) is not added because hosts may have both. Popcon counts installations, mostly pulled in as dependencies, not direct parser use. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'xml' (9 hits, 1 of them a C XML parser) plus seven targeted C names; Conan and Debian miss vendored single-file parsers. The control oracle (controls/xml/check_controls.py) uses Python's pyexpat, the same family as expat but not libxml2, so the libxml2 match is a cross-family check. The expat harness pins XML_SetHashSalt so AFL++ maps are reproducible; libxml2 needed no such change. ISO C documents no XML API. Two valid UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, encoding, XML 1.1 or rejection behaviour.

Pilot cell: Xerces-C++ 3.3.0 and pugixml 1.16 were built and control-verified. Homebrew install-on-request (365d) orders the four differently: tinyxml2 1,757, pugixml 1,270, Xerces-C++ 1,209, libxml++ 461, so the order depends on the metric; Debian dev installs remain the one primary metric. Source-level popcon is not used because libxml++2.6's 79,794 count is a runtime pulled in by dependents (79,361 with no recent file access). tinyxml2 and libxml++ stay unresolved leads in leads.json. libxml++ parses through the libxml2 C library. Whole frameworks (Qt, Boost, POCO) were not ranked. The ISO C++ standard library has no XML API. pugixml does no namespace processing: its namespace-resolved output comes from adapter code over pugixml's qualified names, so namespace well-formedness is checked by the adapter, not the library. pugixml also skips DOCTYPE without expanding DTD entities. Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity declaration, validation, non-UTF-8 encoding or XML 1.1 behaviour; attributes are reported sorted per element because DOM NamedNodeMap order is unspecified.

Pilot cell: only the highest Imported-by XML parser lead (github.com/beevik/etree, 2,098) was built and control-verified. etree tokenizes with encoding/xml.Decoder.RawToken, so it shares the Go encoding/xml tokenizer family with the unranked standard path; only its tree building and namespace lookup are separate code. 15 further numeric leads are logged in leads.json and are not selected or ranked. Renderers, HTTP clients, Office/OOXML, SAML/xmldsig, JUnit, libvirt and AWS serializer hits were not treated as leads. The search covers the first 100 hits of six queries ('xml dom' returned 68 and 'xml reader' 28). Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity declaration, non-UTF-8 encoding, XML 1.1, or attribute-value normalization behaviour.

Pilot cell: only the highest-adoption Java XML parser engine lead (xerces:xercesImpl 2.12.2, 2,474 deps.dev direct dependents summed over all releases) was built and control-verified. jackson-dataformat-xml, jsoup and xstream score higher but are a data-binding layer, an HTML parser and a serializer, and are logged as non-parser leads. dom4j (both coordinates summed: 3,189) and JDOM are tree builders over a JAXP SAX parser that defaults to the JDK Xerces fork, so they have no tokenizer of its own. The standard javax.xml.parsers path runs OpenJDK's internal repackaged Xerces fork, so both verified Java XML paths share the Apache Xerces2-J family; they are separate, diverged code copies. The xercesImpl release jar has no line tables, so its pinned sources jar is recompiled with -g for line coverage. DOM keeps no attribute order, so attributes are reported sorted per element. Maven Central text search ranks by relevance, not adoption; leads were looked up directly on deps.dev. Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, schema, non-UTF-8 or XML 1.1 behaviour.

Pilot cell: one third-party path (saxes 6.0.0, 601,886,067 npm downloads 2026-10-17 to 2026-11-15) was built, verified on two valid namespace controls against the expat oracle, and given parser-derived V8 AFL++ feedback. It is the highest-download lead in the snapshot with its own JavaScript XML 1.0 + Namespaces parser and namespace URI resolution; jsdom (587,846,374) delegates its XML parsing to saxes, and htmlparser2 (526,964,241) is an HTML tokenizer with an xmlMode. sax (490,225,823), fast-xml-parser (426,764,010) and @xmldom/xmldom (326,406,305) have their own parsers and were not run. Downloads were fetched for 19 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit; transitive dependency downloads (jsdom pulls saxes) inflate saxes's count relative to direct use. saxes takes strings, so the adapter decodes bytes with a strict UTF-8 TextDecoder first. Node.js 26.10.0 core has no XML parser API. Browser DOMParser is a known web runtime XML API but has not been replayed on the pilot controls, so the verified standard count remains 0 and the browser route is unresolved. Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity declaration, non-UTF-8 encoding, XML 1.1, or attribute-value normalization behaviour.

Pilot cell, one verified third-party path. The earlier zero count wrongly excluded libxml2-family wrappers; PROTOCOL.md lets a wrapper qualify as a package API with its parser family identified, so sabre/xml is counted with family libxml2 (shared with the standard XMLReader path). symfony/dom-crawler and jms/serializer stay excluded because they only navigate or map an already parsed DOM/SimpleXML tree. The other libxml2-family wrappers (veewee/xml, mtownsend/xml-to-array, saloonphp/xml-wrangler, laravie/parser, orchestra/parser, pear/xml_parser and smaller ones) were not evaluated by the cutoff and remain unresolved, as do the own-code leads prewk/xml-string-streamer and watoki/dom. sabre/xml drops xmlns declarations and text in mixed-content elements by design, so its summary omits namespace declaration counts. Its coverage image uses Ubuntu PHP 8.5.4 with libxml 2.15.2; its AFL++ overlay uses the source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4. The search covers the first 100 hits of five Packagist queries; controls are two small UTF-8 namespace-aware documents without DOCTYPE.

This is a one-parser pilot, not a completed registry search or top-ten claim. Nine named leads were inspected from PyPI/project documentation; the bounded PyPI Simple Index search remains pending. Eight third-party leads lack pinned control checks. The standard API inventory currently verifies ElementTree only; Expat, DOM and SAX API paths remain documented leads. xmltodict and ElementTree share the Expat syntax engine. The valid control exercises a common XML 1.0 subset, not full XML 1.0 conformance. PyPI Stats package downloads are not XML-specific use.

Pilot cell: one verified path, chosen as the highest crates.io 90-day download count (178,628,779) among search hits that are XML parsers. Higher-ranked or comparable hits that are not XML parsers (windows, pulldown-cmark) are excluded. 16 XML parser leads remain unverified (top: xmlparser 52,247,004, roxmltree 42,073,295, xml-rs 32,180,109), so the count of one reflects pilot scope, not a search result. Search covers only the first 100 hits of seven queries (642 hits, 483 unique) captured 2026-11-17; the 'xml' query alone reports 5931 matches. Recent downloads include transitive dependency pulls and are an adoption proxy. Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, external entity, non-UTF-8 encoding, XML 1.1, or attribute-value whitespace normalization behaviour.
